The outcome and signed receipt echo both identifiers; the receipt also binds version_id and control_key_digest so the accepted control state remains auditable. Creating a new Organization DID is a separate inception ceremony and has no member here. Idempotency is per generation: replaying the current generation's byte-identical request returns created=false, while a request after revoke, or one that changes local_admin_subject or the scope set, opens registration_generation+1 with created=true. This operation registers a reference and local administrative delegation only: it does not host the DID's method history, make this deployment the controller, or create Realm, membership, notary, capability or service delegation.

Issue a single-use control challenge for an external, already-published Organization DID. The request MUST carry stable organization_id as did_core_id and the current published did; before issuing the challenge the registry independently resolves and validates did with the registered method adapter and requires project(did)=organization_id. The response challenge echoes and binds both identifiers together with purpose, audience, origin, trust domain, nonce, requested scopes, beneficiary local_admin_subject and a window of at most 300 seconds. Two phases are mandatory: the registry remembers this challenge, then ensure supplies a method-native proof over the same control transcript. Folding the challenge into ensure would let the caller supply its own, defeating freshness and single use. The challenge MUST be consumed on first successful use. Deliberately not idempotent: every call mints a fresh nonce, and the caller MUST prove against the newest challenge.

Re-prove control at a newer resolved version and re-issue the receipt, returning created=false. The request MUST carry stable organization_id as did_core_id and the current published did; the receiver independently resolves and validates did with the registered method adapter and requires project(did)=organization_id. The fresh challenge and method-native control transcript bind both identifiers plus the refreshed version_id/log_head_digest. The refreshed outcome and signed receipt echo organization_id and did and bind version_id and control_key_digest. A same-core did refresh updates resolution/control state, not identity. Scopes are not renegotiated here; a scope change is a new ensure. Refresh exists because a binding pinned to one version stops proving current control after controller rotation and a first-time proof must not authorise the relationship indefinitely.

Withdraw the local binding by stable organization_id did_core_id only, returning the current binding outcome with a receipt whose status=revoked and created=false. No did is required because revoke addresses the already-bound local identity rather than resolving or proving fresh external control. This local act does not modify, deactivate or annotate the external DID's method history. revoked is terminal for the generation; re-establishing the relationship requires a fresh ensure with did, a new challenge and a new control proof.

Read the local binding by stable organization_id did_core_id without creating or mutating state; returns created=false. The outcome includes the current published did and signed receipt, with project(did)=organization_id and receipt/control-state bindings defined by OrganizationRegistrationOutcome and OrganizationRegistrationReceipt. Only bindings the caller is authorised to manage or see are returned. A caller with no such authorisation MUST receive the same not-found answer as for an organization that was never registered, so the query cannot enumerate which organizations a deployment has bound.

Publish a signed ak.schema.recovery_policy.v1 genesis policy or rotation as a Principal Control Realm ak.policy.set EventInitialSubmission. The canonical Event payload is {policy_id,value}; value is the complete RecoveryPolicy, both policy ids MUST match, and state/reason MUST be absent. Event actor/scope, value.principal_id, lease and accepted control Seal MUST agree. The command returns success only after the Event is covered by the immutable acceptance_basis; before Seal materialization it returns retry-safe frontier_unavailable for the same Event id.

Read the currently accepted ak.schema.recovery_policy.v1 projection for the authenticated or explicitly selected principal. Returns active_policy=null when no accepted policy exists; does not publish, rotate, or revoke policy state.

Creates one durable recovery session owned by the exact recovery_session grant id and cnf.jkt presented as Authorization: DPoP plus matching DPoP. request_id, canonical create intent, candidate device, principal, audience and grant coordinates are immutable. Same request identity plus identical intent returns the retained session; a different intent or reuse of one grant for another session fails duplicate_conflict.

did_authority.when: proof_kind == did_root and the accepted PCR recovery policy explicitly enables the factor

operations.notes: Requires the exact recovery_session grant id and cnf.jkt frozen by create. Proof transcript binds request_id, grant id, cnf.jkt and the complete recovery session tuple. Exact proof replay returns the retained verified outcome; another proof intent after terminal transition fails closed.

Idempotently return or create the service identity bound to the canonical (service_kind, public_base_url) registration key. The client supplies did plus the client-controlled signed did:webvh inception operation; the Provider verifies the proof, requires state.id=did, projects did to the returned service_id did_core_id, and never receives private key material. Provider persistence MUST enforce UNIQUE(service_kind, public_base_url) and MUST reject an existing hosted document that declares the same key even when the mapping row is absent.
Read the service registration bound to the canonical (service_kind, public_base_url) key without creating or mutating identity state.

High-assurance optional endpoint to revoke a previously issued cursor authority. Revocation hits return cursor_revoked and MUST NOT advance account subscribe position, barrier wait, or dropped recovery state. To-device queue deletion is decoupled from cursors entirely and happens only via ak.self.device_messages.command.ack.v1.

Carries exactly one holder-signed profile_event EventInitialSubmission and no unsigned patch. event.realm_id is the exact account-local PCR Realm selector; accepted-profile presence is evaluated only in that PCR lineage. If it has no accepted Actor Profile, the Event must be ak.profile.create; its actor_profile ID is derived by retyping the create Event ID and payload.object must omit id. If it has an accepted Profile, the Event must be ak.profile.update, payload.target_ref must equal that create-derived ID, and the signed patch remains limited to display_name, avatar_blob_ref and profile_fields.<key>. Both branches bind realm scope to the same PCR and event.actor_id to the session principal. On create payload.object.principal_id must equal that principal; on update the accepted target profile's materialized principal_id must equal it. Direct holder proof is required without executor or Applet provenance. Event preconditions are empty; update concurrency uses only optional signed payload.expected_state_digest. The service forwards the exact bytes through ordinary Event admission without authoring, rebuilding, co-signing, choosing an ID or adding a concurrency guard. Until the Control Move has accepted Seal coverage the operation returns frontier_unavailable; exact retry after coverage returns the byte-identical stored outcome. The single accepted effect advances the holder account-aggregate projection once; it creates no Directory announcement or account-data Event.

Holder-bound one-shot read of the current principal account projection. Returns principal_id, account lifecycle state, device summaries, optional ActorProfile, and signed handle-claim evidence or refs. Because the operation has no account-local-lineage selector, profile is present only when exactly one accepted profile is unambiguous across the principal's PCR lineages; multiple accepted lineages fail closed by omitting profile, never by choosing an implicit current PCR. It MUST NOT return an unsigned bare handle as authoritative identity. Naming: the trailing segment 'viewer' is intentionally outside the api-conventions.md §2.4 read-verb taxonomy; it follows the GraphQL 'viewer' convention (the authenticated subject's own projection). The target is located by the holder-bound session rather than an external id, so 'get' does not apply, and 'viewer' (subject identity projection) stays distinct from 'describe' (service capability metadata).

Streaming push of cross-Realm account-aggregate deltas (cross-Realm frontier, to_device queue, account_data, device_lists, unread / notification counts). Signal envelopes use the Signal Extension live rail and are not account aggregate state. Connection is long-lived; server pushes NDJSON frames as new data becomes available.
Lists the authenticated actor's account_data entries. content is stored verbatim and is opaque to the server.

Submits the caller-signed tombstone ak.account_data.set Event. The actor-private cell subject is composite[envelope.actor_id, payload.key], so only the holder may sign it and the service MUST NOT author it under its own DID. expected_revision is the Event payload's; it is no longer a query parameter. deletion_mode=value_tombstone keys MUST still be refused here.

Reads one account_data entry by account_data_key key, including its compare-and-set revision. Returns not_found when the key is unset or holds a tombstone; the not_found error.details carry account_data_cas_conflict_details so the caller still learns current_revision.

Builds a ak.account_data.set actor-private write as a compare-and-set whole-value replacement: expected_revision must equal the accepted revision (0 to create) and the stored revision becomes expected_revision + 1. A mismatch returns cas_conflict with account_data_cas_conflict_details and stores nothing, so a stale offline retry can never overwrite a newer write. Controller-private registered types reject agent / applet / service principals. content is stored verbatim; clients own canonical encoding and (for sensitive keys) client-side encryption.

Consume an agent-provisioning abandonment challenge and explicitly give up an accepted ak.agent.provision whose declared managed Agent PCR genesis will never be submitted (zh/identity/key-management.md section 3.6.3). Authenticated by the controller user_session; the presented credentials MUST be fresh and MUST NOT be the ones presented when the challenge was issued, while re-authentication strength, risk checks and cooldown are deployment governance. One transaction consumes the challenge, releases the agent_slug selector claim and the principal_control_realm_id claim, records the tombstone / audit reservation and suppresses every holder-readable trace of the allocation; any step failing means zero writes. If the genesis was accepted between issuance and confirmation the request MUST fail with agent_pcr_genesis_already_accepted and MUST NOT abandon anything, because an established Agent is retired through ak.self.agent.command.deactivate.v1. Replaying the same request_id returns the same terminal outcome and MUST NOT produce a second tombstone. The accepted provision Event stays in the controller PCR history and the abandoned realm id MUST NOT be reused.

Issue the single-use challenge that authorizes explicitly abandoning an accepted ak.agent.provision whose declared managed Agent PCR genesis was never accepted (zh/identity/key-management.md section 3.6.3). Authenticated by the controller user_session. The service requires agent_id, principal_control_realm_id and allocation_handle to equal the authenticated controller's accepted provision, and MUST refuse to issue a challenge once that genesis is accepted. The <=300s single-use challenge is bound to the controller account_subject, holder key, agent_id, agent_slug, the declared principal_control_realm_id, the allocation, the closed consequence disclosure, audience, origin, trust domain, purpose and expiry. Repeating the same request_id returns the same unconsumed challenge. Challenge state MUST be shared durable state, not process-local memory; expiry and prior consumption are distinct terminal states. This operation abandons nothing by itself and MUST NOT be reachable from lease expiry, garbage collection or any automated flow.

Controller-only caller-signed ak.capability.revoke Control Move. Path grant_id, payload grant_id/grant_ref, path Agent subject, target Realm, authenticated actor, the exact account-local lineage selected by the session, and the sole signed head_eq guard on the complete grant-cell head are all admission invariants. The service never authors the Event or appends CAS after signing; exact replay returns event.created_at as revoked_at.

Controller-only full replacement of one Account-Authority-owned per-scope selection. The authenticated bearer+DPoP session is the authority proof. First write uses expected_version=0; each accepted write increments the exact agent/scope slot by one. Governance ceilings and ordinary Agent capabilities are evaluated at action time and are not copied into this record.

Prepare fixes the new|existing branch, every reducer-derived coordinate, Event ID, canonical unsigned Event bytes and digest. It returns two controller-signing drafts for a new Sidecar and only an attach draft for an existing Sidecar. Commit accepts only proofs appended to those exact drafts. First ensure atomically admits exactly [ak.sidecar.create, ak.sidecar.context.attach]; attach must reference the reserved create Event with role after. The parent-Realm bootstrap exception is scoped only to create.

Controller-only paginated Sidecar list, optionally filtered by realm_id. Returns only Sidecars owned by the authenticated controller and never ordinary Circles or another controller's existence stubs.

Controller-only dedicated Sidecar read surface. Returns the typed Sidecar plus read-only owned/effective Agent sets, native MLS context and reconciliation readiness. Unauthorized, nonexistent, and foreign-controller IDs use one indistinguishable not_found envelope.

Only outward carrier for the PCR-resident ak.profile.create / ak.profile.update facts. A global profile Event lives in its owner's Principal Control Realm, so a co-member cannot reach it through a Realm-scoped read and MUST NOT reach it through a cross-principal actor selector on ak.self.events.read.scan.v1. Authorization is current effective joined membership of body realm_id for both the caller and each returned actor; realm_id MUST NOT be a Principal Control Realm. Each row returns the exact signed profile Event and the accepted Seal covering that one event_digest, and never any other Event of that Realm. Unknown actor, actor without an accepted profile, non-member actor and unauthorized caller all report profile_unavailable so the operation cannot probe membership or account existence.

Closed selector XOR. current_admission binds the actual operation, request digest, verifier, audience and challenge and may authorize first live Signal evidence through current shared context. historical_event binds Event id, digest and receiver service and returns only the destination-signed admission receipt persisted when that exact Event was accepted; current state never reconstructs historical validity.

The active Applet service submits only Realm, exact external tuple, and optional display input. The Principal Server derives every current registration, grant, registration-epoch, package, hosting, and time coordinate, atomically supersedes any prior uncommitted generation for the same branch subject, and returns the exact persisted signed authoring request.

durable_effect.rationale: No Event is admitted, but the Principal Server durably records the current subject generation and exact signed request before returning
No Event is admitted, but the Principal Server atomically persists the branch-subject winner, exact unsigned payload, exact signed request, and superseded generations before returning

operations.notes: The Applet service consumes the one signed install_bot or provision_ghost authoring request and returns the exact role-neutral four-Event bundle. Its durable ledger is keyed by branch subject plus full signed-request digest and preserves exact request/bundle bytes, actor key handle, method history, and provision state. No derived request ID or branch-specific Event aliases exist.

durable_effect.rationale: The operation admits no Arkret Event; independently, the Applet service atomically persists the subject/request-digest ledger, exact request and bundle, actor key custody, method history, and provision state before returning

operations.notes: Read-only pre-admission of final signed Events followed by one authority-issued publication lease per Event. The operation never commits an Event or advances a frontier. Ordinary Events bind an accepted seal_ref/seal_basis; only complete registered genesis units may bind the ordered anchor_unit digest. Idempotent retry returns byte-identical leases.

Query parameters are realm_id, subject, required subject_principal_server_id and optional at. subject plus subject_principal_server_id form the exact PrincipalAuthorityKey; no local-service, bearer-service, DID-document or delivery-binding fallback is allowed.

Issues a short-TTL, single-blob, read-only pre-signed URL whose authorization material rides in the URL itself (query string). Used as a deliberate carve-out of the no-credentials-in-URL rule (server-threat-model.md S21) so that browser primitives like /

Media service token exchange operation. Issues a short-lived (TTL <= 600s) backend_token + participant_binding for joining a focus declared in ak.realm.media_service.foci[]. Same wire across all backend kinds (livekit / mediasoup / janus / arkret_native); only backend_token shape is backend-specific. Token issuer DID MUST be one of the Realm-authorized media service DIDs; clients reject otherwise (token_issuer_unauthorised). See zh/crypto-media/media-service-binding.md §3.

Submits the caller-signed ak.circle.archive Event carried in lifecycle_event through ordinary Event admission; payload.target_ref MUST name the path Circle. Transition follows the Circle lifecycle matrix (reducer rejects illegal transitions with circle_not_active). The service MUST NOT co-sign, rebuild or synthesize the Event.

Submits the caller-signed ak.circle.create Event carried in create_event through ordinary Event admission; the parent Realm is create_event.event.realm_id. The Circle id is retype(create_event.event.event_id), so the service MUST NOT mint it, and MUST NOT co-sign, rebuild or synthesize the Event. Reducer-locked fields (mls_group_id, state) MUST NOT be actor-supplied; encryption_profile='none' is allowed only when the parent Realm policy floor permits plaintext.

Submits the caller-signed ak.circle.restore Event carried in lifecycle_event through ordinary Event admission; payload.target_ref MUST name the path Circle. Transition follows the Circle lifecycle matrix (reducer rejects illegal transitions with circle_not_archived). Restore re-enables new writes after pending MLS membership removals are settled. The service MUST NOT co-sign, rebuild or synthesize the Event.

Rotates the Circle's bound MLS group. MUST NOT acknowledge a rotation without actually changing the cryptographic scope; returns unsupported_feature until the MLS genesis/commit/welcome cascade is wired end-to-end.

Submits the caller-signed ak.circle.tombstone Event carried in lifecycle_event through ordinary Event admission; payload.target_ref MUST name the path Circle. Terminal: the lifecycle matrix admits no transition out, so the signed Event is the whole record of who ended the Circle. Response surfaces the terminal state with empty members. The service MUST NOT co-sign, rebuild or synthesize the Event.

Submits the caller-signed ak.circle.member.state Event carried in member_event through ordinary Event admission; payload.circle_id MUST equal the path circle_id. Moving another actor to join requires ak.circle.member.manage narrowed to this Circle, evaluated against projected grants rather than asserted by the request, and the target MUST already be a joined parent-Realm member (strict-subset invariant); a self-join is gated by join_rule. The service MUST NOT co-sign, rebuild or synthesize the Event, nor add a capability verdict to the closed payload.

Submits the caller-signed ak.circle.member.state Event carried in member_event through ordinary Event admission. The Event membership MUST be leave and payload.expected_membership MUST carry the concrete current membership as its signed head_eq guard; payload.circle_id and payload.actor_id MUST equal the two path identifiers, and event.realm_id MUST equal the path Circle's parent Realm. Removing another actor requires ak.circle.member.manage narrowed to this Circle. The service MUST NOT co-sign, rebuild or synthesize the Event.
Lists Circles the caller may see within one parent Realm (required realm_id query). Directory visibility is enforced per Circle; non-members of a 'members'-visibility Circle MUST NOT see it.
Reads one Circle projection. Returns not_found when the Circle is invisible to the caller rather than disclosing existence.

Submits the caller-signed ak.consent.grant Control Move carried in grant_event through ordinary Event admission. payload.consent_id is the producer-allocated cell subject and the or_set add dot is 'ak:event:<enclosing event_id>:<write_index>', so the service chooses neither and MUST NOT synthesize the Event. The authenticated actor MUST be authorized to write the holder's consent (holder or an explicitly authorized controller/agent).

Submits an opaque consent-contact request from the authenticated peer. peer_principal_id defaults to and MUST equal the actor. The response is identical for missing holders, policy denial, rate limiting, silent drop and quarantine acceptance; the operation never returns a consent cell.

Submits the caller-signed ak.consent.revoke Control Move carried in revoke_event through ordinary Event admission. Its payload.observed_dot_ids MUST enumerate the active grant dots being removed for the (consent_id, peer, consent_scope), read back from consent_cell_view.active_grant_dots. Revoking consent_scope=any cascades all concrete scopes and MUST still enumerate every dot; revoking a concrete scope leaves others intact.
Lists holder-private consent cells for the authenticated holder only. Peer actors MUST NOT receive cell state, dots, expiry or request timestamps.
Reads one holder-private consent cell. The authenticated actor MUST equal holder_principal_id or be an explicitly authorised holder controller; peers never receive this DTO.

Holder-authorized deterministic compaction of the oldest contiguous terminal Contact prefix. The server computes the core from accepted history; callers cannot submit or choose it. Cross-service pairs use the continuity_checkpoint branch of ak.peer.contacts.command.submit.v1: the receiver recomputes, countersigns, durably commits and returns the complete checkpoint in one round trip, then the proposer commits the exact returned bytes. Exact replay returns the same checkpoint; same sequence with another digest is continuity_invalid and has no winner. Export reuses continuity_evidence on ak.self.contact.read.list.v1 and import reuses the Contact request continuity_evidence field.

Two-phase holder-local terminal reject. The service accepts only the holder-signed ak.contact.rejected Event bytes reserved for the exact current request slot, signs the matching rejection acceptance receipt, and provides durable exact replay/conflict semantics independently from normal accept responses.

Two-phase holder-local acceptance of one holder-signed ak.contact.requested fact. The accepted source receipt, peer closed XOR, full directional scope set and issuer-local slot lineage are durable replay inputs; no Private Consent Event is written or consulted. Recontact may import one generic mutually signed bilateral prefix checkpoint plus at most 64 uncompressed tail rounds. Missing material is continuity_evidence_unavailable; invalid, rollback or forked material is continuity_invalid. A new lineage never inherits the old checkpoint, history or audit identity.

Two-phase holder-local normal accept response. The service accepts only the holder-signed response Event bytes reserved for the current request slot, signs the matching normal-response acceptance receipt, and never writes Private Consent. Reject uses the separate ak.self.contact.command.reject.v1 operation. Glare is mechanically derived from two causally concurrent request receipts and forbids this operation.

Two-phase prepare/commit carrier for one holder-signed ak.contact.scope.update full-set directional replacement. Request/response establishes the issuer-local version 1 genesis; every scope replacement is version >= 2, exactly current+1, and references the exact issuer-local current head. Expansion and narrowing are both explicit signed replacements.
Holder-signed issuer-local lineage terminal. It consumes the Contact round and generation; it does not carry scope replacement and does not write or revoke Private Consent.

Holder contact projection from source-signed request/response receipts, issuer-local Contact lineages and current signed head leases. An accepted row carries the next_prepare_input cursor and, after bilateral compaction, the exact portable continuity_evidence checkpoint plus bounded tail; this is the only export surface. A pending_incoming row carries the complete signed request_acceptance_receipt for respond or reject. Every other contact_state omits unavailable authoring/evidence fields. Private Consent and account-data notes are never Contact authority.

Issue one immutable current-authority authority Ack for a fully signed Control Move. Local device/Agent authorities use the same typed request and outcome without an HTTP hop. A caller canonically sorts distinct authority Acks and may submit the resulting receipt set only when the current notary profile quorum and common-window rules are satisfied.

Authenticated submission of one complete signed_defer or signed_reject. The receiver loads the durable accepted proposal and its immutable canonical ControlProposalAck, recomputes proposal_ack_digest, verifies the exact Realm/proposal/authority-set/deadline/defer chain and quorum, then atomically persists the decision. Exact decision replay is byte-identical duplicate; conflicting terminal or post-Seal decisions fail closed. For ak.device.revoke, only a valid signed_reject for the exact proposal/Ack (therefore the exact reducer-derived device and generation) clears that proposal's revocation_pending record; it clears no other pending revoke for the device.

Authenticated exact proposal observation surface. Returns only the durable authority discriminator, canonical Ack when applicable, verified decision chain and covering Seal state for the requested Realm/proposal digest. control_proposal_ack permits the closed pending/deferred/overdue/rejected/sealed chain and always carries Ack; the narrow ackless_event_proof branch permits only pending/sealed and carries no Ack, decision or Ack-derived deadline fault. ak.device.revoke is always control_proposal_ack. The operation cannot mint an Ack, synthesize a reject or mutate pending state; unauthorized and unknown selectors are non-enumerating.

Explicit, cumulative, monotonic to-device delivery acknowledgement (client-sync.md §10.1). Queue deletion happens only here; stream cursor advancement (account subscribe after=, device_messages after=) is read-only and MUST NOT prune the queue. Re-acking the same or an older token is a legal no-op. Unknown / expired / cross-bound tokens are rejected with param_invalid (reason invalid_ack_token) without deleting anything.

Enqueues caller-supplied DeviceMessageEnvelope targets into recipient device queues. The sender's exact durable device/generation state is checked in the queue transaction; revocation_pending returns device_revocation_pending and enqueues nothing. Each target carries a sender-assigned device_message_id copied unchanged into the stored envelope; the service deduplicates logical messages by (sender_principal_id, sender_device_id, device_message_id), returning the existing outcome for identical canonical target content and duplicate_conflict/device_message_id_conflict for different content. HTTP batch replay is additionally deduplicated by (sender, Idempotency-Key). Queue pruning is only via ak.self.device_messages.command.ack.v1.

Query-only resolver for the pair's single stable Direct Conversation. It never creates. An encrypted DC has one immutable scope-derived MLS group and monotonic epoch lineage; the response carries exact current group_state_ref+digest. Repair is an ordinary Commit in that group. If all private group state is lost, the old DC Realm is terminal and a new conversation requires a new Realm id. No second group, epoch reset or timeout takeover exists.

Initial durable Event publication uses EventInitialSubmission: the signed Event remains the only business fact, while AuthorizationLease and optional CbaProofBundle values are independently verified publication evidence outside the Event digest. Before accepting a device-authored Event or appending principal_server_admission, the origin Principal Server reads the exact durable device revocation state in the same admission transaction; revocation_pending returns device_revocation_pending and zero Event/proof writes. Accepted ak.device.revoke is Ack-required and atomically writes its derived exact device/generation pending record. For a locally authored Realm Event, canonical acceptance, the complete distinct recipient-service target set and every target outbox intent commit atomically. A missing route creates durable pending_route and never rejects the Event; each send rechecks the frozen exact member/delivery-binding authority, authority loss terminally cancels the old target, and submit exposes only pending_delivery_count; clients derive delivery state as pending iff the count is non-zero. The ingress MUST persist and return the original IngressReceipt before lease expiry; byte-identical retry returns the stored receipt without changing received_at. For ak.invite.claim, the receiving Realm reducer remains the authoritative state machine and re-checks token commitment, allowlist, replay, proposal and expiry state. The direct_conversation_founding branch remains its closed four-Event atomic unit: Realm create, peer membership join, main Strand create and founder membership join. The agent_membership_cascade branch is the only controller-cascade carrier: atomic_self_leave accepts the controller terminal Event and the exact pre-state Agent leave set all-or-nothing; emergency_terminal accepts a third-party terminal Event and atomically freezes a durable exact-set cleanup intent without synthesizing Agent Events; emergency_cleanup accepts only the same initiator's complete signed Agent leave set and commits it atomically. Effective Agent membership is invalid immediately after the terminal transition, independent of cleanup completion. Exact replay returns the original byte-identical outcome, while the same cleanup intent with different canonical content is duplicate_conflict.

PCR-only pre-sign preparation for one exact prospective successor Seal. The receiver requires the exact current predecessor frontier and exact accepted uncovered Control Event set, derives the sole eligible holder from the accepted PCR genesis ak.realm.create principal_server_id after validating its principal_server_admission and historical signer evidence, chooses sealed_at, issues and durably stores every required AvailabilityReceipt plus authenticated holder-signer evidence, and returns every-and-only dependency with canonical digests. It fails closed when the local Principal Server is not that create-locked holder, the default min_holders=1 contract cannot be met, or any requested basis is stale or incomplete. The response is preparation material only and does not commit a Seal.

Submit one client-signed Seal directly. A Seal is not an Event and never uses EventInitialSubmission. Except for the canonical genesis exception, the signature MUST satisfy predecessor governance notary actor/threshold rules. The receiver recomputes Seal id, recursive coverage, completeness_root, state_root, signer authority and signature.

Return the complete durable frozen fanout target set for one caller-visible accepted Event. Unknown and invisible Events share not_found. Rows use stable opaque target_id and are sorted byte-wise; service_id is included only when the caller can currently read an exact contributing member delivery-binding. The query has no retry, route-resolution or delivery side effect.
Actor/data Event causal frontier only. actor_id is required; Realm Seal discovery is exclusively ak.self.seals.read.frontier.v1.
Realm Seal frontier discovery. Returns the complete canonical accepted Seal antichain, governance health and observation coordinate.

Exact Seal-only resolve by seal_refs. Event selectors are forbidden. Optional self history_traversal_access names one retained request receipt/archive replica basis digest and authorizes only Seal refs in its exact target-to-base traversal cut; unknown and unauthorized remain indistinguishable.

Near-current stateless group_security_frontier query only. The caller binds exact proof_base_basis and proof_target_basis antichains plus the closed frontier selector. Bulk or old history uses receipt-bound direct accepted-Seal traversal through standard Event/Seal/dependency resolve.

Resolve a caller-split batch of exactly three content-addressed evidence kinds: AvailabilityReceipt, AuthenticatedSignerResolutionEvidence, and MinimalMetadataMlsLeafSignerEvidence. Optional self history_traversal_access is the sole retained-cut visibility exception. The operation is cursor-free and returns no partial result when the complete same-shape outcome exceeds byte_limit or 8 MiB.

Dereference exact event_id/event_digest selectors. Optional self history_traversal_access authorizes only delta Control Moves in one retained target-to-base direct traversal cut and is mutually exclusive with ordinary timeline visibility. Point lookup is not a range scan and never attaches covering/first-activation Seals; Control-Move effectiveness uses Seal frontier/resolve.
Canonical safe and idempotent Events range scan. HTTP uses RFC 10008 QUERY with typed JSON content.

Long-lived per-Realm / actor event stream with optional bounded catch-up replay. `dropped` and `resync_required` control frames MAY carry `reconnect_after_ms`, a server-directed minimum delay before opening another subscription for the same caller/selector scope; early reconnects are rejected with rate_limited / Retry-After.

Authorized account-internal resolution audit evidence: PCR realm id, genesis Event and receipt, current and bounded predecessor resolution Events, and an accepted Seal covering the disclosed state. Authorization is only a current holder session bound to the exact principal_authority pair; recovery first completes the existing recovery transaction and becomes the current holder rather than introducing a second audit authorization path. Unknown account, wrong authority pair and unauthorized caller share one anti-enumeration outcome. history_depth is the closed range 0..256 with default 0 and MUST NOT be silently capped; after_resolution_event_ref stops the disclosed segment exclusively at a known ancestor in this account's lineage and requires history_depth >= 1. A truncated segment sets history_complete=false and returns next_audit_cursor; omitted history is unknown, never absent.
Issues a fresh opaque locator for the authenticated principal. subject_id and recipient_id are server-derived; the raw bearer token is returned exactly once and MUST NOT be persisted.
Idempotently revokes one locator owned by the authenticated principal. A same-principal retry returns the original revoked_at. Unknown, consumed, or cross-principal locator ids return not_found.

Atomically revokes one authenticated-principal-owned locator and issues a new opaque token. The old token becomes indistinguishable from unknown tokens before success is returned. After an uncertain transport outcome, the client MUST first idempotently revoke the old locator_id and only then issue fresh material; directly issuing without that revocation can leave the old token active.

Read the authenticated subject's private invite-receive policy. Returns the recommended default when no explicit override is stored; the response is never written into the target Realm durable event log.

Replace the authenticated subject's private invite-receive policy. The body MUST set subject_id equal to the session actor; the override shares the same store as ak.self.contact.command.tombstone.v1(block_peer) denied_subjects writes.

Transaction-bound monotonic erasure of the exact old secret_storage and mls_history series reserved by a SecurityRotationTransaction. Partial outcomes persist per series/object; exact retry never resurrects or rewrites an erased item. A complete outcome carries the sole canonical erase confirmation.

Issues the durable, single-use, short-TTL (<=300s) challenge that every high-risk backup delete proof must sign over. While a challenge for the same (principal_id, backup_id, request_id) is still valid the service returns the same challenge; a different request_id mints a new one. See key-management.md section 7.8.1.

High-risk delete guarded by a server-issued single-use challenge and the shared high-risk authority proof family (key-management.md section 7.8/7.8.1). The challenge is consumed atomically with the first successful delete; a byte-identical retry returns the stored terminal outcome, and the same request_id with a different canonical digest is a duplicate conflict.

Session-authenticated entry to the canonical KeyPackage claim carrier. The participant supplies the same closed device|native_agent requester_authorization and stable service_binding with source/destination service DIDs used by peer claim; deployment trust domains are absent from participant-authored bytes and are bound only by the Principal Server's verified resolution plus outer RFC 9421 headers. The local Principal Server verifies the current durable requester authorization and exact current membership delivery binding; local source=destination uses the same destination-authority CAS, while remote targets are durably relayed without rewriting the participant-signed body. Uncertain outcomes are queried by the original claim_request_id and request digest before any exact resend.

Carries exactly one direct-holder signed report_event EventInitialSubmission and no unsigned report fields. The Event kind is ak.self.moderation.report; this self endpoint accepts only absent/self provenance and forbids source_provider, delegated executor, Applet and MIMI-facade provenance. event.actor_id and payload.reporter must equal the authenticated session principal. There is no path Realm: event.realm_id, payload.realm_id, signed scope_ref and the accepted target's derived governance scope must match exactly. Realm-default reports may omit payload.effective_scope; Circle reports must sign the exact Circle scope. The target must be accepted and visible to the reporter; absent, invisible and scope-mismatched targets use the same not_found response. This DataEvent carries seal_ref plus auth_context and cannot carry seal_basis or preconditions. The service forwards exact signed bytes through ordinary Event admission and never authors, rebuilds, co-signs, maps an operation ref to another target or adds a concurrency guard. report_id is derived by retyping the accepted Event id and the stored submit outcome has status=submitted. Exact replay returns that byte-identical outcome without a second log or queue append; the same Event identity with different bytes returns duplicate_conflict. routed_to is omitted for an ordinary reporter and may be returned only when the caller independently holds moderation/governance capability for the exact scope.

Authorization-gated data-plane observation returning the exact durable franking proof Event, its target Event, the first covering signed Seal, an RFC 6962 inclusion path against data_event_set_root, and historical service signer evidence. It never substitutes a control-plane delta proof.
Extension read surface listing reducer-maintained Morph lifecycle rows for a Realm. This is a derived read model, not a canonical truth source.

Optional extension read surface returning the authorized document body, version, relation, comment, and cursor-presence read-model for a single document Morph addressed within its Realm. Canonical truth remains the Morph/Relation/Message event history.

Canonical HTTP binding is POST /_arkret/self/policy/check. Paths carry no version segment; protocol version and exact carrier support are discovered via *.describe / supported_operation_bundles (see sync/api-conventions.md).

Accepts exactly one caller-signed ak.read_cursor.advance actor-private Event. The Event payload is the complete ak.schema.read_cursor.v1 cursor; envelope.actor_id and payload.actor_id MUST equal the authenticated holder, payload.device_id MUST equal the authenticated session device, and envelope.realm_id MUST equal payload.realm_id. The service validates and forwards the exact Event bytes and MUST NOT mint the cursor id, choose updated_at, rebuild the payload or co-sign. Multi-device convergence is causal-first per zh/discovery/read-receipts.md section 6.5: a position that causally dominates the other wins regardless of HLC; HLC max applies only to causally concurrent positions, and device_id lexicographic order only breaks equal HLCs. The cursor is never published into shared Realm history.
Lists the authenticated actor's read markers, optionally filtered by the realm_id query param.
Reads only the profile-private submit/read/review/cancel/invite-consume audit trail for one application. Applicant, eligible reviewer, or explicitly authorized Realm auditor only.
Candidate-profile private applicant cancellation. The caller and detached receipt signer must both be the original applicant.

Candidate-profile private reviewer decision. The reviewer-signed receipt binds the exact application revision and a capability grant/frontier proof; stale, expired or unauthorized decisions fail closed.

Candidate-profile private application intake. The applicant-signed receipt binds the accepted knock, policy/revision/private-body digests and applicant DID. The receipt and private body commit atomically and never enter shared Realm history.
Lists candidate application metadata. Reviewers and each matching applicant receive the protected body; other Realm members receive only application_pending placeholders.
Reads one candidate application for its applicant or an eligible reviewer. Every successful private-body read emits ak.audit.accessed.
Returns the organization-inherited effective moderation policy view: inheritance chain, organization policy layers, the Realm's own override, and merged effective rules.

Carries exactly one caller-signed ak.realm.moderation_policy EventInitialSubmission. The request contains moderation_policy_event and no unsigned policy projection; the closed Event payload contains only value, whose value is the complete policy object. event.realm_id must equal the path Realm, event.actor_id must equal the authenticated session actor, and the exact submitted bytes pass ordinary Event admission without service authorship, rebuilding, co-signing or precondition injection. The Event carries exactly one signed head_eq against ak:cell:ak.component.realm.moderation_policy.v1:null naming the complete settled value or null when absent. Admission follows the capability registry and accepts ak.realm.moderation_policy or ak.policy.manage; Realm ownership alone grants no write authority. Organization-approval constraints and any extra action capability required by policy contents are evaluated during admission. Exact byte replay of an accepted Event returns the byte-identical stored outcome; identity/body conflict, stale head, Bottom or multiple applicable CAS guards fails closed with zero additional writes.
Full event-log + operation dump for a Realm (schema ak.export.realm.v1). Caller must be authorized to read the Realm; payload visibility still follows Realm policy.
Reads the Realm lifecycle projection (owner + members + deleted). Returns not_found when the Realm is invisible to the caller.

Submits the caller-signed ak.realm.link Control Move from realm_id -> target_realm_id; the service MUST NOT co-sign, rebuild or synthesize it. The edge is event.payload and the source Realm is event.realm_id, which MUST equal the path realm_id. General directed cycles are valid and traversal uses a visited set; admission rejects only self-reference, invalid kind, invalid payload, or an illegal FSM transition. Self-reference returns schema_violation with reason_code realm_link_self_reference; an illegal transition returns failed_precondition with reason_code realm_link_invalid_transition.

Returns the merged effective policy after walking governed_by / inherits_policy_from ancestors per the Realm's ak.realm.inheritance_policy. inheritance_mode=none when no inheritance policy is projected (implicit inheritance is forbidden).
Lists typed cross-Realm links projected from ak.realm.link. direction is outbound/inbound/both; link_kind_allow is a comma-separated allowlist of canonical link kinds.

Submits the caller-signed tombstoning ak.realm.link Move (payload.status=tombstoned) for the (realm_id, target_realm_id, link_kind) triple; the service MUST NOT co-sign, rebuild or synthesize it. link_kind is named in the signed payload rather than a query parameter, because a query parameter is outside the bytes the caller signs; payload.target_realm_id MUST equal the path target_realm_id. Removing an edge is the same durable Event kind as creating one, so this operation keeps its event_log effect.

Returns the projected ak.realm.organization relationship statements for the Realm (active / revoked / expired, latest-per-(organization_id, relationship)) plus declared owning_organization_ids hints with no verified statement. The caller must be authorized to read the Realm. A relationship is only verified when lifecycle_phase=verified_active; declared_organization_hint_ids are unverified claims and MUST NOT be rendered as official / governed / endorsed.

After ak.policy.manage admission, a settled direct declaration is deleted by the caller-signed durable ak.realm.policy_server Move with the exact payload {"tombstone":true} and head_eq for the complete declaration; the service MUST NOT co-sign, rebuild or synthesize it, which is why this DELETE carries a request body the way ak.self.keys.backups.resource.delete.v1 already does. The registered cas_register effect sets that value in the per-Realm cell; effective reads then ignore the direct binding and resume governed_by fallback or local-only capability evaluation. Repeating DELETE against a settled tombstone is an idempotent empty success and MUST NOT change the cell or state_root. A never-written or inherited-only direct cell returns not_found and MUST NOT mutate an ancestor.
Reads the projected ak.realm.policy_server config. Returns not_found when neither the Realm nor its governed_by ancestor chain declared one. from_organization_fallback=true marks an inherited config.

Submits the caller-signed durable ak.realm.policy_server declaration Move (admission capability ak.policy.manage); the service MUST NOT co-sign, rebuild or synthesize it. The declaration is event.payload and the Realm is event.realm_id, which MUST equal the path realm_id. Reducer validates the DID, canonical HTTPS policy-check URL and on_timeout enum. When the direct cell already has a settled declaration or tombstone, the Move MUST carry head_eq for that complete value and the caller attaches it, because preconditions are inside the signed bytes; an absent direct cell is the only initial write.

Continues only the next step derived from the transaction kind and accepted-step prefix length. request_digest and prepared_plan_digest MUST equal the resource, while expected_accepted_step_count MUST equal the current prefix length; the endpoint is not a generic step or Saga executor. Client attestation is required only for issue_terminal_receipt or local_commit and must bind transaction/request/plan plus the pre-reserved output_ref. When all coordinator-owned steps are accepted but the device is offline, terminal_result remains absent; device-attestation readiness is a computed view of the canonical next step and no coordinator phase/state is serialized.

Creates exactly one durable RecoveryTransaction or SecurityRotationTransaction. The coordinator MUST atomically persist canonical request bytes, request_digest, the closed typed prepared_plan and prepared_plan_digest, all reserved public ids, and the initial resource before the first irreversible side effect. Recovery create also CAS-binds one already verified recovery session to this transaction. Same transaction_id plus identical bytes returns the recorded resource; different bytes returns duplicate_conflict.

Authoritative durable progress query by transaction_id. It MUST return the prepared plan, accepted step prefix and optional terminal result; callers derive the next action from kind plus prefix length. It MUST NOT synthesize progress from a short-lived HTTP idempotency cache.

Encrypted-only Signal Extension send rail for ak.schema.signal_envelope.v1. Exact signal type and product target remain inside ciphertext. It MUST NOT persist the envelope as a durable Event or advance actor_seq / Realm frontier.

Authenticated encrypted-only Signal Extension receive rail. Frames carry SignalEnvelope objects or bounded transport control frames; exact signal type and product target remain inside ciphertext. No catch-up or durable delivery guarantee.
Extension read surface listing reducer-maintained Space lifecycle rows for a Realm. This is a derived read model, not a canonical truth source.
Extension read surface listing reducer-maintained Strand lifecycle rows for a Realm. This is a derived read model, not a canonical truth source.

Create one immutable scope-private history request. The operation envelope may be at most 1 MiB, while the inner HistoryKeyRequest itself is independently capped at 64 KiB canonical bytes. Before success the service verifies the caller-pinned bootstrap/current bases and complete durable target cut, atomically pins every Seal, delta Control Move and registered dependency through request expiry, freezes the exact direct traversal intent, durably stores request/receipt bytes, generates a 32-byte CSPRNG response capability and returns its byte-stable HPKE-sealed carrier. Exact duplicate returns the first byte-identical accepted outcome; different intent under the same request_id conflicts.

List immutable current-member-only requests for the exact Realm/Circle scope. realm_id is required; circle_id absence selects Realm scope. The RRK-holder branch returns only requests whose ranges intersect an archive sealed to the caller's exact historical key.

Durably enqueue one immutable manifest or independently sealed chunk. Manifest admission first resolves and replays the receipt-retained direct Seal/Event/dependency cut, derives current requester incarnation, join floor, winning MLS transitions and current monotone history_access, and atomically writes the all-ranges admission or nothing. A chunk requires that accepted admission, then enforces current T1 and writes the recipient record plus attestation. Premature/mismatched chunks are dependency_missing with zero pending state. Exact duplicate returns the first byte-identical small accepted HistoryKeyResponseSendReceipt.

Capability-addressed sequence-ordered response-stream read. Authorization: Arkret-History-Capability carries the only external locator and authorization value; unknown, expired, garbage-collected and unauthorized capabilities are same-shape not_found. One merged stream contains normal records and signed lost descriptors; ack_token commits every ordered {sequence,kind,response_id,entry_digest} through the page high-water cursor.

Capability-protected contiguous high-water ack. Every covered sequence requires a durable installed, cryptographically_rejected, superseded_duplicate or signed service_record_lost disposition. Manifest installed means descriptor installation only; no reject/lost/manifest disposition completes epoch coverage.

Recipient-bound byte-paged archive list. Query and cursor bind scope/key tuple, accepted evidence Event, complete holder_trusted_basis, holder authority and last ordering tuple. Every row carries the exact holder-accepted archive_replica_digest plus archive-lifetime direct traversal retention for its singleton epoch. The holder MUST use that digest as the closed SelfHistoryTraversalAccess coordinate and may resolve every Control Move/Seal/dependency required by that replay, including membership/policy/control metadata; archive/traversal digests, unrelated DataEvents and generic timeline scan are forbidden substitutes. Unknown/unauthorized/tuple mismatch is same-shape not_found.

Private S2S fanout of one byte-identical request+receipt to a closed exact current member delivery-binding service or exact RRK holder service with intersecting archive tuple. Destination authorization, TTL and bytes are signed; no public Event/DeviceMessage.

Private S2S relay of the immutable source record plus SourceRelayAttestation from the source's authenticated current local Principal Server to request_receipt.release_id. Destination validates the relay service against current source delivery/authority binding and performs the only final T1/release linearization. The two-service cut is not globally atomic; v1 assumes honest services and bounded TTL observation.

Near-current S2S group_security_frontier query only. It binds exact base/target Seal antichains and the closed selector; bulk or old history uses receipt/replica-bound direct Seal traversal through standard Event, Seal and governance-dependency resolve.

Authenticated S2S exact resolve of exactly three content-addressed evidence kinds: AvailabilityReceipt, AuthenticatedSignerResolutionEvidence, and MinimalMetadataMlsLeafSignerEvidence. Omitted history_traversal_access uses ordinary Realm/federation visibility; the optional pending_archive_replica branch is the sole retained-cut exception. Member request replicas never authorize traversal. Unknown, unauthorized, outside-cut and missing selectors are same-shape; complete bounds failure returns no partial items or cursor.

Private immutable RRK archive replica to exact holder_id. It binds exact archive bytes, container Event, accepted evidence Event, complete holder_trusted_basis and archive-lifetime direct traversal retention for one epoch. First durable acceptance assigns one archive_sequence per semantic key; changing replicated_at cannot add a row. Exact duplicate returns the first byte-identical accepted receipt. Archive and replay closure are retained for the Realm recovery-material lifetime; v1 defines no remote GC/renewal.

risk_tier_definitions.low: Read, projection, discovery, ack, and account-private affordances. Freshness fail-closed treats unknown / stale as local-pending allowed (capabilities.md §18).
risk_tier_definitions.medium: Object create / update / delete, message authoring, invite issuance, MLS proposal, audit query. Freshness requires recent frontier within freshness_required_ms.
risk_tier_definitions.high: Capability mutation, policy mutation, lifecycle freeze / tombstone / destroy, schema redefinition, MLS commit / welcome / genesis, audit export, moderation decision, admin / hierarchy / upgrade. Freshness MUST be within freshness_required_ms; partition forces local pending with no peer visibility.

registry_rules: Wire capability grant.actions[] entries MUST be drawn from this registry; wildcards / segment globs are statically rejected by capability-grant.schema.json.

Receivers MUST default to risk_tier=high when an action submitted in a grant or evaluated in policy is not present in this registry; this is the freshness fail-closed default required by capabilities.md §18.

required_constraints lists typed-constraint shorthand names that the capability evaluator MUST enforce for the action regardless of the grant author's declarations; absence in this list does NOT disable other declared constraints.

required_evaluator_checks lists non-grant-field invariants (for example actor_eq_target_author or audit_pair_required) that admission control MUST enforce from Event context, reducer state, or paired audit evidence. These are not grant-constraint schema fields.

target_event_kinds links the action to one or more ak.* event_kinds in event_kind_registry. Empty array means the action authorizes a read / projection / signaling path that does not produce a durable reducer-input event. Reducer admission for a listed event_kind MUST verify the actor holds at least one matching action grant.

profile is null for v1 core actions, or a ak.profile.*.v<n> id when the action is only meaningful inside that profile. Receivers without the named profile MUST treat the action as unknown (risk_tier=high default).

Every action MUST declare event_mapping_kind. action == single target_event_kind uses same_name; empty target_event_kinds uses non_event_surface; any other mapping MUST use one of the allowed deviation categories.

grant_authority_actions lists the action ids an issuer holding this action MAY sign a grant for (capabilities.md section 3.2 issuer upper bound). It is a separate namespace from target_event_kinds, which only expresses direct Event admission: several actions can map to one event kind, so an event-kind subset MUST NOT be used to satisfy an action-level grant authority question.

coverage_rule and grant_authority_rule declare how target_event_kinds and grant_authority_actions are derived from the other rows. When a rule is present the materialized list is a cached projection: tools/artifact_pipeline.py generate rewrites it and check rejects any hand edit on either this registry or the generated view.

root_control_only=true marks an action that only the current controller of the Realm authority-root cell may author. It is never grantable and never enters a derived owner authority set. subject_only=true marks a self-service action whose only authority is the target subject's own signature. reducer_only=true marks a record the reducer materializes and no principal may author. The three flags are orthogonal and combinable.

actions.notes: Authorizes only actor_role=ghost ak.applet.managed_actor.provision inside the closed four-Event Ghost unit: provision, applet_managed_control PCR genesis, accountability grant and profile create. The conditional Event admission and operation validator require the exact active registration/grant/scope and atomic set.

Reducer-materialized record of a Realm-link inheritance derivation (zh/models/realm-links.md section 6). No principal authors it and no principal can be granted it, so it is excluded from every derived owner authority set.

Subject-only self-service release of the actor own grant. Authority comes from the target grant subject signature and the reducer target guard, never from a capability, so it is excluded from every derived authority set.

Read-only audit access for a Realm admin NOT in the target Circle. MUST be paired with ak.audit.accessed event. Does NOT yield historical decryption keys unless the admin is formally added to the Circle.

Creates an intra-Realm Circle (scoped event/message boundary; optionally MLS-backed depending on parent Realm floor). NOT in default member bundle by default — Circles should be few and stable. See zh/models/circle.md §8.
Manage an existing Circle. MUST be constrained to specific circle_id selectors; unconstrained Realm-wide grant is not a normal management permission.
Self-service: actor accepts an invite, joins a join_rule=open Circle, or leaves. Reducer enforces payload.actor_id == envelope.actor_id and transition legality. Self-unbanning MUST fail closed.
Cross-actor write (rare). MUST carry ak.audit.accessed pair (same model as ak.strand.watch.set.others).
Invite / remove others. Held by Circle admin. payload.actor_id != envelope.actor_id.

Authorizes only the transaction-bound old-series targets in a fixed SecurityRotationTransaction plan after both replacement active-series pointers are accepted. It never authorizes deleting an active or unplanned backup series.
Direct Conversation participant self-leave only. It never authorizes leave/ban/remove of the other participant or any join transition.

Accepted-at compensation for a self-authored join only. It authorizes one fresh standard leave transition for the exact admission and old membership incarnation; it cannot be transferred or used as ordinary membership authority.

Accepted-at compensation for a delegated/admin-authored join only. It authorizes one fresh standard remove transition for the exact admission and old membership incarnation; it grants no Realm admin capability.

Direct Conversation exact-pair self-rejoin only. It never authorizes a first join, a third participant, or a join authored on behalf of the other participant, and it never authorizes any grant, policy, admin, Strand or binding change.

Authorizes adding an audience_mention node such as @all or @here to a Message create/revise. @here maps to audience="strand_engaged" and is not presence-filtered. This is an additional gate: the actor MUST also be authorized for the underlying message create/revise action. Effective Realm/Circle policy MUST allow the audience and declare finite max_recipients/quota before notification fanout.

Authorizes a decrypted ak.message.stream Signal payload for one discussion Strand. It is an additional recipient-verified gate: the sender MUST also hold ak.message.create. The service cannot inspect or advertise the encrypted payload kind or Strand target.

Narrow Direct Conversation participant authority for welcoming another currently authorized device of the same stable participant. It cannot add a third principal or a device of the other participant.
Authorizes reading an object's discussion / history events (message timeline, redacted-message metainfo, prior revisions). Read / projection surface only; emits no durable reducer event.

Claims, renames or tombstones the Realm's human-readable alias (ak.realm.alias event; projects ak.component.realm.alias.v1). high risk because an alias is the address users type and share: capturing or re-pointing one is a phishing / impersonation primitive. Holding ak.realm.admin (aggregate admin coverage) satisfies admission, or grant this specific action directly. See zh/discovery/object-addressing.md §3.3.
Advances the authority generation, invalidating every grant anchored to the previous one at read time. Destructive root control; never grantable.

Terminal Realm lifecycle. Authored only by the current controller of the Realm authority-root cell with an independent destructive confirmation; it MUST NOT be granted to anyone, so it is excluded from every derived owner authority set.

Highest explicit authority inside one Realm. Held either by the current controller of the ak.component.realm.authority_root.v1 cell (root authority, not a grant) or by an ordinary revocable co-owner grant. Both derived sets are rule-generated; hand edits are rejected by tools/artifact_pipeline.py check.

Rotates the controller binding of the Realm authority-root cell. Authored only by the current controller with successor acceptance; it MUST NOT be granted, so it is excluded from every derived owner authority set.

Sets / changes the Realm's authoritative default discussion Strand pointer (ak.realm.set_default_strand event; projects Realm default_strand_id). Same-name discipline. The Realm authz gate is realm-admin: holding ak.realm.admin (aggregate admin coverage) satisfies admission, or grant this specific action directly. Reducer MUST verify the referenced Strand already exists (failed_precondition otherwise). See zh/models/strand-and-message.md default-Strand discovery section.
Terminal Realm lifecycle with a successor pointer. Same root-control family as ak.realm.destroy: authored only by the current authority-root controller and never grantable.
Holder-private consent is authored only by the current controller of the holder Principal Control Realm; it is never grantable to a Realm co-owner or another principal.
Holder-private consent revocation is authored only by the current controller of the holder Principal Control Realm and must remove caller-observed dots; it is never grantable.

registry_rules: A calendar schedule MUST carry a signed tzdb_version naming one release row below. Receivers resolve timezone and every derived instant with that release, never with their locally installed release.

Release rows are append-only and each row is frozen once published, including its own required_normalizations table, because historical schedules signed that row. Withdrawing a release is expressed by setting status=deprecated, never by deleting or rewriting the row.

required_normalizations is per release, not global. A later IANA release that changes a Link target expresses that by carrying a different mapping in its own row; the earlier row keeps the mapping that was in force when those schedules were signed. A global table could not represent both at once and would silently break the append-only promise.

Determinism comes from the release tag: IANA tzdata release tags are immutable once published. This registry deliberately does not mirror the full Zone/Link table and does not pin a distribution digest, because a hand-copied mirror would drift from IANA and become a second truth source, and this repository cannot verify third-party distribution bytes. Deployments that additionally need supply-chain pinning verify the distribution in their own build; that pinning is out of scope for v1 interop.

Canonicalization is defined by the Link declarations of the pinned IANA release as published by IANA, in particular its backward and etcetera files: the canonical Zone is the Link target. It is NOT defined by whatever a given platform time zone library happens to expose, since distributions may build the same release with different link handling.

Producers MUST rewrite timezone to the canonical Zone before signing. Receivers MUST NOT re-canonicalize a signed value: an alias that reaches the wire is a producer defect and MUST be rejected, not repaired. The RSVP occurrence key reuses the exact signed timezone value.

Each row required_normalizations is the conformance-required subset that vectors pin for that release. It is not the full alias set; an input outside the table is still canonicalized by that release Link declarations.

Updating a schedule tzdb_version MAY change derived instants but MUST NOT change the signed timezone value or any local occurrence key. When any occurrence instant or end changes, the significant-change table requires RSVP needs_reconfirmation plus a schedule notification.

A service that cannot execute a schedule tzdb_version MUST fail closed with calendar_tzdb_mismatch or unsupported_feature, or mark instant projection unresolved. Falling back to a nearby or newer release is forbidden. Services declare their executable set in ServiceDescribe.calendar_tzdb_versions.

releases.notes: v1 conformance baseline release. Frozen: this row required_normalizations is the mapping schedules pinned to 2025a were signed against.
Appended release; schedules pinned to it expand with its rules only. Its required_normalizations is identical to 2025a because no listed Link target changed between the two releases.

registry_rules: Only an active adapter row can validate a did or project it to did_core_id. DID syntax alone never admits a method.
project is a method-defined semantic transform over a canonical bare did, not generic string concatenation or prefix removal. Receivers compare the complete projected did_core_id byte-for-byte.

Every adapter validates method-native control, deactivation, currentness and history evidence according to its trust profile before returning a verified projection. Unknown methods and unknown adapter versions fail closed.

A new did is an update of an existing principal or service only when the same active adapter projects it to the identical did_core_id. A method or core change creates a new identity and cannot inherit authorization through a continuity assertion.
DID URLs are constructed and compared from the verified did under the adapter's DID URL rules. A did_core_id is never used as a DID URL base.

No adapter exposes expand or core_to_did. Even when a method-specific suffix appears reversible, an isolated did_core_id cannot create resolution authority; the required did or did_url arrives through did-evidence-boundary-registry.json.

A did is a canonical bare DID and therefore contains no path, query or fragment. Each active adapter deterministically emits method_history_head, version_id and service_resolution_event_ref according to its registered rules, including synthetic values for methods without native history.

For a generic Event proof, the verifier extracts the canonical bare did base from proof.verification_method, validates the active adapter and key at the cited accepted-at method history, projects that did, and compares the resulting did_core_id to executed_by when present or actor_id otherwise. registration_anchor and pcr_recovery are the only registered special admissions and never convert current DID control into generic human PCR authority.

A principal resolution update is admitted only in its derived identity-control Realm and only when one exact head_eq precondition guards ak:cell:ak.component.identity.resolution.v1:null. The guarded whole resolution_projection MUST equal the accepted current cell; predecessor event/history coordinates come only from that signed precondition, never from payload mirrors.

predecessor_rules: precondition.value equals the accepted current resolution_projection field for field
payload.next is a method-valid successor of precondition.value.method_history_head

portable.relocation_rule: A successor whose canonical host-and-path differs from the accepted predecessor is valid only when the predecessor's effective portable value is true and every method-native successor check succeeds. Missing or false rejects relocation; setting portable=true only in the relocating successor cannot authorize that same relocation.

watchers.rule: The adapter validates and retains watchers as method-native canonical data, but v1 never uses it for authorization, admission, controller selection, witness quorum, freshness, routing or policy. Unknown shape still fails under the method parser; presence, absence or contents cannot grant authority.

supported_features is the only public runtime feature claim set. Registry status describes lifecycle and never creates a second advertised set.

semantic_guarantees: Agent runtime approval transitions emit the normative user-visible notification surface.
Detached JWS inputs and verification results follow the canonical Arkret detached-signature transcript.
The deployment supports the explicitly relaxed E2EE policy branch defined by the normative encryption contract.
Eligible members can execute the normative private history-key recovery protocol.
Identity resolution verifies and serves the native did:webvh log contract.
Invite addressing accepts only the registered introduction kinds and advertised maximum-behavior policy.
Message bodies accept the versioned Content Block structural contract.
Application encryption derives AEAD material through the registered MLS exporter labels.
MLS epochs are fully bound to the accepted Arkret governance frontier.
Last-resort KeyPackages follow the replay, consumption, and rotation rules of the normative MLS contract.
The deployment can emit the normative notification projection without implying push transport support.
Realm service-resolution state is mirrored with the normative authenticated frontier semantics.
